segments.text: Six months after my diet ended, I tried on the dress I wore to my sister's wedding,
and the zipper stopped halfway up my back. Same dress, same mirror, and I felt like everything I
had worked for was gone. That night I sat on the bedroom floor in the dress, half zipped,
staring at the wall, to a shame to tell my sister the dress did not fit anymore, so I said nothing.
Then one morning, over coffee, I read something that changed everything. A study had followed people
for a full year after their diet, and their hunger was still louder, their fullness still weaker.
I wrote four words down in my notebook. It was not me. So I started again, smaller this time,
eggs for breakfast, water before coffee. A walk after dinner, every single night, no matter the weather.
Three months later, I danced all night at the wedding in that dress, and this time I knew why it would
hold. Save this for the day you want to quit and start again.
